games.title: Blood Metabolites Measurement and Their Applications: quick quiz
games.topic: Blood Metabolites Measurement and Their Applications
games.blurb: Quiz for Year 2 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which of the following blood metabolites is the primary marker used for the early biochemical diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction?
questions.explanation: Cardiac troponins are the gold standard biomarker for myocardial necrosis due to their high cardiac specificity and sensitivity.

questions.q: An elevated fasting blood glucose level combined with which of the following metabolites is characteristic of untreated type 1 diabetes mellitus presenting with ketoacidosis?
questions.explanation: Untreated type 1 diabetes leads to lipolysis and excess ketone body production, predominantly beta-hydroxybutyrate, causing high anion gap metabolic acidosis.

questions.q: In the evaluation of renal function, which blood metabolite is derived non-enzymatically from muscle creatine and serves as the basis for estimating glomerular filtration rate?
questions.explanation: Serum creatinine is produced at a relatively constant rate from muscle creatine and is filtered by the glomeruli, making it a key marker for renal function.

questions.q: A patient presents with jaundice, right upper quadrant pain, and markedly elevated serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST). This biochemical profile is most consistent with:
questions.explanation: Marked elevations of transaminases (ALT and AST) reflect acute damage to hepatocytes.

questions.q: Which blood metabolite measurement is essential for monitoring long-term glycemic control over the preceding 2 to 3 months in a patient with diabetes mellitus?
questions.explanation: HbA1c reflects the average plasma glucose concentration over the lifespan of an erythrocyte, approximately 8 to 12 weeks.

questions.q: An elevated serum uric acid level is the primary biochemical abnormality associated with which of the following clinical conditions?
questions.explanation: Hyperuricemia leads to the precipitation of monosodium urate crystals in joints and tissues, resulting in gout.

questions.q: Which of the following lipid profile metabolites is considered protective against atherosclerosis and coronary artery disease?
questions.explanation: HDL-C is responsible for reverse cholesterol transport, carrying cholesterol from peripheral tissues back to the liver, and is inversely correlated with cardiovascular risk.

questions.q: In a patient presenting with acute epigastric pain radiating to the back, measurement of which blood metabolite is most crucial for establishing the diagnosis of acute pancreatitis?
questions.explanation: Serum lipase is more sensitive and specific than amylase for the diagnosis of acute pancreatitis.

questions.q: An increase in blood urea nitrogen (BUN) out of proportion to serum creatinine (BUN:Cr ratio > 20:1) is the classic biochemical finding in:
questions.explanation: Prerenal azotemia (such as in volume depletion or heart failure) leads to increased tubular reabsorption of urea alongside sodium and water, elevating the BUN:Cr ratio.

questions.q: Which of the following blood metabolites is measured in an arterial blood gas (ABG) panel to directly assess tissue hypoperfusion and anaerobic metabolism in shock?
questions.explanation: Blood lactate rises significantly when oxygen delivery is inadequate, forcing cells to rely on anaerobic glycolysis.

games.title: Heart Disease — Must Knows: quick quiz
games.blurb: Quiz for Year 3 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most common cause of left-sided heart failure?
questions.explanation: Systemic hypertension increases left ventricular afterload, leading to hypertrophy and eventual left-sided heart failure.

questions.q: What is the hallmark microscopic finding in the myocardium 1 to 3 days following an acute myocardial infarction?
questions.explanation: Days 1 to 3 post-infarction are characterized by coagulative necrosis and a dense infiltration of neutrophils.

questions.q: Which form of cardiomyopathy is characterized by disproportionate ventricular septal hypertrophy leading to left ventricular outflow obstruction?
questions.explanation: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy typically features asymmetric septal hypertrophy causing subaortic outflow obstruction.

questions.q: In infective endocarditis, which valve is most commonly affected in intravenous drug users?
questions.explanation: Intravenous drug users introduce pathogens directly into the venous system, making the tricuspid valve the most frequently infected.

questions.q: Which major Jones criterion is associated with rheumatic fever?
questions.explanation: Sydenham chorea is a major Jones criterion, whereas arthralgia, fever, and elevated ESR are minor criteria.

questions.q: What is the primary hemodynamic consequence of cardiac tamponade?
questions.explanation: Fluid accumulation in the pericardial sac restricts ventricular expansion, severely impairing diastolic filling.

questions.q: Which type of angina occurs unpredictably at rest and is caused by coronary artery vasospasm?
questions.explanation: Prinzmetal angina is caused by transient coronary artery vasospasm leading to ischemia at rest.

questions.q: What is the most common primary cardiac tumor in adults?
questions.explanation: Myxomas are the most common benign primary cardiac tumors in adults, frequently located in the left atrium.

questions.q: Which histological change is characteristic of chronic passive congestion of the liver secondary to right-sided heart failure?
questions.explanation: Chronic passive congestion causes centrilobular congestion and hepatocyte loss, creating a 'nutmeg liver' appearance.

questions.q: Which coronary artery is most commonly occluded in acute myocardial infarctions, earning it the title 'widow-maker'?
questions.explanation: The left anterior descending artery supplies the anterior wall and apex of the left ventricle, and its occlusion is clinically termed the widow-maker.

games.title: Bleeding Disorders: case showdown
games.blurb: Case Showdown for Year 4 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with a 3-day history of scattered petechiae and easy bruising without systemic symptoms. Physical examination shows no hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy. Laboratory tests show a platelet count of 14 x 10^9/L, normal hemoglobin and leukocyte counts, and normal PT and aPTT. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Isolated severe thrombocytopenia with normal coagulation studies and an otherwise unremarkable blood count in a young adult is characteristic of immune thrombocytopenia (ITP).

questions.q: A 19-year-old woman presents with severe menorrhagia since menarche and frequent epistaxis. Her laboratory studies show a normal platelet count, normal PT, slightly prolonged aPTT, and a significantly prolonged PFA-100 closure time. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: von Willebrand disease typically presents with mucosal bleeding, a prolonged platelet function analyzer (PFA-100) closure time, and variable prolongation of the aPTT due to reduced Factor VIII carrier capability.

questions.q: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the clinic due to painful right knee swelling following minor trauma. Laboratory testing demonstrates an isolated prolonged aPTT of 65 seconds (normal 25–35) that fully corrects upon a 1:1 mixing study with normal plasma. Which coagulation factor assay is most appropriate to check first?
questions.explanation: Hemarthrosis combined with an isolated prolonged aPTT that corrects on mixing study strongly points to an intrinsic pathway factor deficiency, most commonly Factor VIII (Hemophilia A).

questions.q: A 34-year-old woman presents with confusion, fever, and a widespread petechial rash. Laboratory findings reveal a hemoglobin of 7.2 g/dL, platelets 11 x 10^9/L, abundant schistocytes on blood film, elevated creatinine, and normal PT and aPTT. What is the most urgent next step in management?
questions.explanation: The clinical presentation of fever, neurological changes, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, and thrombocytopenia indicates Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP), which requires immediate therapeutic plasma exchange.

questions.q: A 64-year-old man in the intensive care unit for Escherichia coli septic shock begins oozing blood from central line sites and surgical drains. Laboratory results demonstrate a platelet count of 35 x 10^9/L, prolonged PT and aPTT, decreased plasma fibrinogen, and markedly elevated D-dimer. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Severe sepsis triggering generalized microvascular thrombosis and consumption of platelets and clotting factors (low fibrinogen, high D-dimer, prolonged PT/aPTT) is classic for Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC).

questions.q: A 58-year-old man receiving unfractionated heparin for deep vein thrombosis experiences a 55% drop in platelet count on day 6 of therapy. He is clinically stable without active bleeding. What is the immediate next best step in management?
options: Switch from unfractionated heparin to low-molecular-weight heparin
Transfuse 1 unit of random donor platelets
Continue heparin and recheck platelets in 24 hours
questions.explanation: Suspected Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT) requires immediate cessation of all heparin products and initiation of a non-heparin parenteral anticoagulant such as argatroban to reduce thrombotic risk.

questions.q: A 72-year-old man who has been receiving prolonged broad-spectrum oral antibiotics for a chronic wound infection develops spontaneous ecchymoses. Laboratory evaluation reveals an isolated significantly prolonged PT/INR (INR 3.2) with a normal platelet count and normal fibrinogen. What is the most appropriate initial treatment?
questions.explanation: Prolonged antibiotic use suppresses vitamin K-producing gut flora, leading to an isolated prolonged PT/INR due to depletion of factor VII, which is rapidly reversed by vitamin K.

questions.q: A 75-year-old woman presents with new, spontaneous, extensive soft tissue hematomas without any prior personal or family history of bleeding. Laboratory testing demonstrates an isolated prolonged aPTT of 78 seconds that fails to correct after a 1:1 mixing study with normal plasma. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Late-onset spontaneous hematomas with an isolated prolonged aPTT that does not correct on a mixing study indicates the presence of a factor inhibitor, most commonly an acquired autoantibody against Factor VIII.

games.title: Wk 4 portal hypertension: case showdown
games.blurb: Case Showdown for Year 4 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: A 54-year-old male with known alcoholic cirrhosis presents to the emergency department with massive hematemesis and melena. On arrival, blood pressure is 85/50 mmHg, heart rate is 120 bpm, and two large-bore intravenous lines are placed for fluid resuscitation. What is the most appropriate next medical therapy to initiate prior to urgent endoscopy?
questions.explanation: In suspected acute variceal hemorrhage, vasoactive agents such as octreotide or terlipressin should be started immediately alongside prophylactic antibiotics prior to endoscopy.

questions.q: A 61-year-old female with decompensated liver cirrhosis presents with low-grade fever, diffuse abdominal tenderness, and mild confusion. Diagnostic paracentesis is performed, yielding cloudy fluid with a neutrophil count of 350 cells/mm³. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
questions.explanation: An ascitic fluid neutrophil count of 250 cells/mm³ or greater confirms spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, requiring prompt IV antibiotic therapy such as a third-generation cephalosporin.

questions.q: A 48-year-old male presents with increasing abdominal girth and lower extremity edema over 3 weeks. Abdominal paracentesis reveals a serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG) of 1.4 g/dL and total protein of 1.8 g/dL. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's ascites?
questions.explanation: A high SAAG (≥ 1.1 g/dL) combined with low total protein (< 2.5 g/dL) strongly indicates portal hypertension secondary to liver cirrhosis.

questions.q: A 52-year-old female with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis undergoes a screening upper endoscopy, which demonstrates medium-sized esophageal varices with red wale signs. She has no prior history of gastrointestinal bleeding. What is the most appropriate management to prevent initial bleeding?
questions.explanation: Primary prophylaxis for medium-to-large esophageal varices involves non-selective beta-blockers (e.g., propranolol) or endoscopic band ligation.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male with a history of recurrent severe chronic pancreatitis presents with an episode of hematemesis. Upper endoscopy shows isolated gastric fundal varices with no esophageal varices. What is the most likely underlying cause of his portal hypertension?
questions.explanation: Chronic pancreatitis can lead to splenic vein thrombosis, causing sinistral (left-sided) portal hypertension and isolated gastric varices.

questions.q: A 58-year-old male with alcoholic cirrhosis and refractory ascites develops progressive acute kidney injury with a serum creatinine rise from 1.0 to 3.2 mg/dL over one week. Urine sodium is < 10 mEq/L, urine sediment is normal, and renal ultrasound shows no structural abnormality. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Hepatorenal syndrome is functional renal failure in advanced liver disease characterized by intense renal vasoconstriction, low urine sodium, and absence of intrinsic renal pathology.

questions.q: A 32-year-old female with polycythemia vera presents with acute right upper quadrant abdominal pain, hepatomegaly, and rapidly developing ascites. Doppler ultrasonography reveals absence of flow in the hepatic veins. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Budd-Chiari syndrome is post-sinusoidal portal hypertension caused by hepatic venous outflow obstruction, commonly associated with hypercoagulable states.

questions.q: A 65-year-old male with NASH cirrhosis is brought to the clinic by his family due to daytime somnolence, disorientation, and flapping tremor (asterixis) on examination. Serum ammonia levels are elevated. What is the first-line medical treatment for this condition?
questions.explanation: Lactulose is the first-line treatment for hepatic encephalopathy as it converts ammonia to non-absorbable ammonium in the gut.

games.title: Virology: drug duel
games.blurb: Drug Duel for Year 3 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which of the following antiviral drugs is a nucleotide analogue of adenosine monophosphate used primarily for the treatment of cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis in immunocompromised patients?
questions.explanation: Cidofovir is an acyclic nucleotide analogue of cytosine, but clinically grouped as a nucleotide analogue of adenosine monophosphate that does not require initial viral phosphorylation and is used for CMV retinitis.

questions.q: What is the primary mechanism of action of Oseltamivir in the management of influenza A and B infections?
options: Inhibition of viral uncoating by blocking the M2 proton channel
Inhibition of viral neuraminidase to prevent the release of progeny virions
Inhibition of viral DNA polymerase by premature chain termination
Binding to hemagglutinin to prevent viral attachment to host cells
questions.explanation: Oseltamivir is a neuraminidase inhibitor that prevents the cleavage of sialic acid residues, thereby trapping newly formed influenza virions on the host cell surface and preventing spread.

questions.q: Which antiretroviral drug class is characteristically associated with metabolic toxicities such as lipodystrophy, dyslipidemia, and insulin resistance?
questions.explanation: Protease inhibitors (such as ritonavir and darunavir) interfere with lipid and glucose metabolism, characteristically leading to central adiposity, hyperlipidemia, and insulin resistance.

questions.q: Which of the following is a recognized and significant dose-limiting side effect of intravenous Acyclovir therapy?
options: Crystalline nephropathy and acute kidney injury
questions.explanation: Acyclovir can precipitate in the renal tubules, particularly when administered rapidly intravenously or in the setting of volume depletion, leading to crystalline nephropathy.

questions.q: What is the principal mechanism of action of Enfuvirtide in the treatment of HIV-1 infection?
options: It binds to CCR5 on the host cell membrane to prevent viral entry
It inhibits the fusion of the viral envelope with the host cell membrane by binding to gp41
It blocks the action of HIV protease, preventing the cleavage of viral polyproteins
It prevents the integration of viral DNA into the host genome
questions.explanation: Enfuvirtide is a fusion inhibitor that binds to the HIV gp41 subunit, conformational changes are blocked, and viral entry into the CD4+ T-cell is prevented.

questions.q: Which hepatitis C direct-acting antiviral drug acts as a non-structural protein 5A (NS5A) inhibitor?
questions.explanation: Ledipasvir is an NS5A inhibitor crucial for viral RNA replication and assembly, commonly co-formulated with the nucleotide analog polymerase inhibitor sofosbuvir.

questions.q: Which characteristic adverse effect is most commonly associated with the long-term use of Zidovudine (AZT), an NRTI used in HIV management?
questions.explanation: Zidovudine inhibits mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma, frequently causing dose-dependent bone marrow suppression that manifests as severe macrocytic anemia and neutropenia.

questions.q: Which drug is categorized as a Non-Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitor (NNRTI) and is well-known for causing central nervous system side effects such as vivid dreams and dizziness upon initiation?
questions.explanation: Efavirenz is an NNRTI that frequently causes transient central nervous system side effects, including vivid dreams, insomnia, dizziness, and psychiatric disturbances.

games.title: Oncology: Surgery, Radiotherapy & Chemotherapy Explained: drug duel
games.blurb: Drug Duel for Year 3 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which anti-neoplastic agent is famously associated with hemorrhagic cystitis, an adverse effect that can be mitigated by co-administration of mesna?
questions.explanation: Cyclophosphamide is metabolized to acrolein, which causes hemorrhagic cystitis, a toxic effect prevented by the uroprotective agent mesna.

questions.q: What is the primary mechanism of action of paclitaxel in the treatment of solid tumors?
options: Hyper-stabilizing polymerized microtubules to prevent disassembly
questions.explanation: Paclitaxel binds to tubulin and promotes microtubule assembly while preventing disassembly, causing cell cycle arrest in the M-phase.

questions.q: A 55-year-old patient undergoing chemotherapy with doxorubicin should be routinely monitored for which dose-limiting toxicity?
questions.explanation: Doxorubicin generates free radicals that cause cumulative dose-dependent cardiotoxicity, presenting as dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure.

questions.q: Which rescue therapy is administered following high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy to protect healthy tissues from severe folate deficiency?
questions.explanation: Leucovorin (folinic acid) bypasses dihydrofolate reductase inhibition by providing a reduced form of folic acid to rescue normal non-cancerous cells.

questions.q: Which chemotherapeutic drug acts specifically by binding to tubulin subunits and preventing their polymerization into functional mitotic spindles?
questions.explanation: Vincristine binds to beta-tubulin to prevent microtubule polymerization, leading to mitotic arrest during the M-phase.

questions.q: Which cytotoxic antibiotic is uniquely associated with dose-dependent pulmonary toxicity, such as pneumonitis and pulmonary fibrosis?
questions.explanation: Bleomycin induces free-radical-mediated DNA strand breaks and causes lung toxicity due to low levels of the inactivating enzyme bleomycin hydrolase in pulmonary tissue.

questions.q: Cisplatin exerts its cytotoxic effect primarily through which molecular mechanism?
options: Formation of inter- and intra-strand DNA cross-links
Blockade of HER2 receptor tyrosine kinase activity
questions.explanation: Cisplatin is a platinum compound that covalently binds to DNA, forming cross-links that inhibit DNA replication and transcription.

questions.q: Trastuzumab is a targeted monoclonal antibody indicated for patients whose tumors express high levels of which protein?
questions.explanation: Trastuzumab specifically targets the extracellular domain of the HER2/neu (ERBB2) receptor kinase present in HER2-overexpressing breast and gastric cancers.
